title: Exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators: a systematic review and directions for future research.
authors: Shea B, Shaman J
abstract: Global routine childhood immunization has stagnated for almost two decades, leaving children vulnerable to both immediate and long-term health risks from infectious diseases. Identifying and mitigating impediments to childhood vaccination, such as barriers resulting from exposure to natural disasters, is vital for maintaining population health. While there is general understanding that disasters have the potential to disrupt vaccination services, well designed studies on the degree to which exposure to natural disasters affects vaccination indicators are limited. Understanding the effects of natural disasters on vaccine preventable diseases is an important area for future research as some natural disasters are becoming more frequent and intense due to climate change. To understand the current state of research on exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators (i.e., vaccination metrics including administration, coverage, rates), we conducted a systematic literature review of all literature in Embase, Google Scholar, PubMed, and Web of Science up until September 11-12, 2025. We aimed to identify relevant peer reviewed literature focusing on natural disasters and immunization and to assess them for relevance and inclusion. Seventeen studies met the criteria for inclusion. These studies examined the relationship between exposure to cyclones/hurricanes, droughts, earthquakes, flooding, heat waves, and multiple disaster types and changes in vaccination among different age groups. Most (16/17 (94.12%)) papers identified a connection or association between exposure to natural disasters and reduced vaccination indicators. The majority (13/17 (76.47%)) of studies focused on early-childhood vaccinations. Characteristics that affect vulnerability to under-vaccination-exposure level, geographical location, socioeconomic status-were assessed in several papers. Areas for future research include quantifying the degree to which different disaster types affect multiple vaccination indicators within the same individuals and changes in communities over time.

title: Novel creatine formulation exhibits similar serum creatine concentrations and pharmacokinetics to creatine monohydrate in healthy adults.
authors: DelBiondo GM, Gottlieb CW, Baker PA, Johnson WM, Kelly CG, Smith-Ryan AE
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: BACKGROUND: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) is the most widely studied creatine form, demonstrating robust efficacy, bioavailability, and safety. With creatine growing in popularity, alternative formulations of creatine have been developed to target solubility and to optimize absorption pharmacokinetics (PK), as well as to reduce gastrointestinal (GI) intolerability. The purpose of the current study was to evaluate the acute effects of a novel creatine monohydrate (OptiCreatineTM; CrO) compared to CrM on serum creatine PK and GI tolerability in healthy adults. METHODS: Healthy, recreationally active adults (age: 22 ± 3 years; males n = 8, females n = 9) consumed a single 5-gram dose of CrM or CrO across two separate visits following an overnight fast, in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Venous blood samples were collected at baseline and 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, and 300 mins post-ingestion of their assigned treatment to assess serum creatine concentrations. PK parameters including peak concentration (Cmax), time to peak (Tmax), absorption rate constant (ka), elimination rate constant (kel; h-1), and area under the curve (AUC₀-T) were derived using nonlinear regression modeling. GI symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires. RESULTS: There was no difference in serum creatine concentrations between CrM or CrO across all participants (p = 0.707), males (p = 0.318), or females (p = 0.996) at any time point. Serum creatine increased over time regardless of treatment (p < 0.0001). No differences were observed between CrM and CrO for Cmax (mean difference ± standard deviation (MD ± SD): 7.66 ± 50.37μM; p = 0.82), Tmax (MD ± SD: -0.04 ± 0.13 h; p = 0.54), ka (MD ± SD: -0.15 ± 0.45 h-1; p = 0.51), kel (MD ± SD: 0.01 ± 0.03 h-1; p = 0.61), or AUC₀-T (MD ± SD: 22.09 ± 160.57 μM·h; p = 0.74), with no sex × treatment interactions (p ≥ 0.05). Descriptive evaluation showed similar GI symptom profiles between conditions, with low frequency and minimal severity reported across both treatments. CONCLUSIONS: A single 5-gram dose of CrO produced similar serum creatine and PK characteristics to CrM in healthy adults. These findings support CrO as a viable delivery option, with no significant differences in acute pharmacokinetic profiles or GI tolerability compared to CrM.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: Differential mortality risks associated with ambient temperature among migrants and non-migrants: a space-time-stratified case-crossover study of the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort (2000-2020).
authors: Firouraghi N, Cortes TR, Jacobson LV, Neves DJD, Silveira IH, Hajat S, Barreto ML, Pescarini JM
abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate change disproportionately affects socially minoritized populations, but migrants' vulnerability to extreme temperatures remains overlooked. We estimated short-term associations between extreme ambient temperatures and mortality among migrants and non-migrants across Brazil. METHODS: We linked the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort to mortality and temperature data (2000-2020) and conducted a space-time-stratified case-crossover study analysing the differential effects of extreme temperature on mortality among internal migrants (i.e., Individuals whose state of birth was different from their residence at registration or death) and non-migrants. We used conditional quasi-Poisson regression with distributed lag non-linear model (DLNM) to estimate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause non-accidental and cause-specific mortality associated with extreme-cold (1st percentile) and extreme-heat (99th percentile) compared to minimum-mortality-temperature (i.e., the temperature associated with the lowest mortality risk), over 0-20 days in both groups. We further stratified by age, literacy, urbanicity and housing conditions. FINDINGS: We included 1,199,636 deaths among internal-migrants (mean age at death = 62.67 years (standard-deviation (SD) = 18.36), with 673,166 (56%) males) and 3,716,900 deaths among non-migrants (57.18 years (SD = 20.31), with 2,135,293 (57%) males). Over 0-20 days, we observed a consistent pattern of higher risks of all-cause, non-accidental mortality among internal-migrants than non-migrants following both extreme-heat (RRMig(95%CI):1.05(1.01-1.10) vs. RRNon-mig:1.01(0.99-1.04)) and extreme-cold (RRMig:1.27(1.22-1.32) vs. RRNon-mig:1.24(1.20-1.28)). Extreme cold-related circulatory mortality (mortality due to diseases of the circulatory system, based on the relevant International Classification of Diseases codes) (I00-I99) was higher among non-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.20-1.45) vs. RRNon-mig:1.41(1.31-1.51)) while heat-related respiratory mortality (J00-J99) was higher among internal-migrants (RRMig:1.32(1.10-1.58) vs. RRNon-mig:1.06(1.00-1.17)), particularly those illiterate (RRMig:1.84(1.25-2.71) vs. RRNon-mig:1.10(0.89-1.36)). Other subcategories showed greater 95%CI overlap. INTERPRETATION: We found internal migrants are likely to experience higher heat-related respiratory mortality than non-migrants particularly low-educated migrants. Our results highlight the need to further consider migrants for targeted climate adaptation policies, with a focus on reducing social inequalities in the place of arrival. FUNDING: The Wellcome Trust.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Access to clinical cancer genomics and precision oncology-based care in North America.
authors: Kumar P, Salawu A, Demichelis-Gómez R, Williams A, Harris AR, Jenkins-Lord BD, Mullangi S, Bajaj RA
abstract: Despite the scientific and technical capacity for precision oncology in North America (Canada, the United States, and Mexico), its implementation is deeply uneven across the region. Our narrative synthesis of precision oncology implementation found that delivery consistently fails at four operational steps: biomarker testing, molecular interpretation, reimbursement, and access to matched standard-of-care therapy or clinical trial. These failures arise along disparity axes that differ by country but converge on a single outcome: patients whose cancers harbor actionable biomarkers do not receive precision oncology-based care. We conclude that precision oncology must be treated as essential cancer-care infrastructure rather than an optional research-based service and propose a tri-national implementation agenda. Acting now is particularly urgent given the rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on precision oncology-derived datasets, which risk entrenching existing inequities into clinical decision-making before implementation reform can catch up.

title: Role of protein lactylation in pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases: Current research and future perspectives (Review).
authors: Pan ZA, Tong LT, Wang ZM
abstract: The cardiopulmonary system is highly coupled in structure and function. Metabolic and epigenetic disturbances constitute the common pathological basis for the progression of cardiopulmonary diseases and their comorbidities. Aberrant metabolic reprogramming triggers lactate accumulation. As a novel post-translational modification, protein lactylation participates in the regulation of inflammatory responses, cell death and fibrotic remodeling, thereby mediating cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Existing studies have separately illustrated the roles of lactylation in isolated pulmonary and cardiac disorders. Nevertheless, most investigations are confined to a single-organ perspective, lacking systematic summaries of common mechanisms for cardiopulmonary crosstalk and comorbidities. The present review summarized research advances of lactylation in various cardiopulmonary diseases, generalized its potential comorbid mechanisms, identified existing research gaps and translational obstacles for targeted therapy and collected lactylation-targeted intervention compounds with potential therapeutic effects reported in basic studies. The present review further outlined prospective research directions focused on spatiotemporal regulation of lactylation, metabolic-immune-epigenetic crosstalk that shapes disease progression, and the identification of specific targets in cardiopulmonary comorbidities, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation for developing precise, broad-spectrum, co-targeted therapeutic strategies for cardiopulmonary diseases.

title: Targeting triple-negative breast cancer: Molecular basis and emerging antibody-drug conjugate strategies.
authors: Feng H, Padala C, Liu B
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) accounts for ~10-15% of all breast cancers and is an aggressive, molecularly heterogeneous subtype associated with poor clinical outcomes and limited targeted treatment options. Consequently, systemic therapy has historically relied on chemotherapy, which is often compromised by recurrence, dose-limiting toxicity, and the rapid development of therapeutic resistance. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as a transformative therapeutic platform by combining tumor-specific antibody targeting highly potent cytotoxic payloads through advances in antibody engineering, linker chemistry, and payload design. This mini-review summarizes recent advances in ADC development for TNBC, with a particular focus on the molecular basis of ADC therapy, the chemical determinants governing efficacy and selectivity, emerging mechanisms of resistance, and next-generation strategies to improve therapeutic durability and clinical outcomes.

title: Mitochondrial pharmacology of cardiovascular and antidiabetic drugs: Mechanistic basis of cardioprotection and cardiotoxicity in the diseased heart.
authors: Kurian GA
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Mitochondrial function is a central determinant of cardiomyocyte survival, yet mitochondrial pharmacology remains under-integrated into cardiovascular and antidiabetic drug classification, safety assessment, and therapeutic decision-making. Many cardiometabolic drugs exert direct or indirect effects on mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, calcium handling, quality control, and genome stability effects that can confer protection in some contexts while precipitating toxicity in others. In diseased myocardium, where mitochondrial reserve is constrained by ischemia, metabolic stress, ageing, or heart failure, these drug-mitochondria interactions frequently dictate clinical benefit or harm beyond the nominal drug class. This review synthesises the mitochondrial actions of widely used cardiovascular and antidiabetic therapies, including statins, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors, β-blockers, metformin, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, and incretin-based agents, across acute and chronic exposure windows. We integrate key mechanistic domains encompassing electron transport chain modulation, redox and cofactor reprogramming, calcium permeability transition coupling, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and stress signalling, and relate these signatures to clinically relevant cardiometabolic disease contexts. We propose a unifying framework in which mitochondrial reserve capacity and quality control competence function as the central decision node determining whether pharmacologic mitochondrial engagement is adaptive or injurious. Finally, we outline principles for mitochondria-conscious prescribing, risk stratification, and drug development, and propose that systematic incorporation of mitochondrial endpoints into clinical trials and safety pipelines is essential for advancing precision cardiometabolic therapy.

title: Anti-USAG-1 therapy for teeth agenesis and biological tooth regeneration: review of current evidence and future directions.
authors: Tawfik AM, Aboulyazeed AM, Abdelsattar RM, Elazizi H, Hazem M, Amer M, Morsi RA, Badr BA
abstract: Hereditary and acquired tooth loss poses a significant challenge for dental patients worldwide. This has led to a lot of research into methods that have alternative teeth loss solutions. One promising area of research is focusing on molecular pathways related to tooth development. Tooth agenesis or the failure to develop teeth is a common developmental dental abnormality. It can manifest as anodontia, where no teeth develop, oligodontia, where a few teeth are missing, or hypodontia, where one or two teeth are missing. This condition can be part of a syndrome or occur on its own due to genetic abnormalities related to tooth development. Recent studies have identified Uterine Sensitization-Associated Gene-1 (USAG-1/SOSTDC1) as a regulator of tooth development. It does this by inhibiting Wnt signaling pathways and Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP). The goal of this review is to provide an overview of the role of the Wnt signalling pathways and USAG-1-mediated tooth agenesis, with a focus on their implications for tooth regeneration. We looked at published research on USAG-1 biology, tooth agenesis genetics and animal studies well as new clinical trials. The evidence shows that tooth agenesis is often caused by mutations in genes, including MSX1, PAX9, WNT10A, AXIN2, EDA etc… Experimental studies have found that inhibiting USAG-1 can awaken tooth germs and improve BMP signaling. Several monoclonal antibodies that target USAG-1 have been discussed. One, antibody #37 showed the most promise in treating hypodontia in animal models. In mice and ferrets, anti-USAG-1 treatment promoted the development of additional or regenerated tooth-like structures and stimulated odontogenic growth. This suggests that BMP signaling plays a role in controlling tooth number. The use of USAG-1 treatment has advanced to Phase I clinical trials in Japan to evaluate its safety and pharmacokinetics. Importantly, current preclinical evidence of anti-USAG-1 mediated tooth regeneration is mainly based on animal models of congenital tooth agenesis, such as hypodontia and oligodontia. However, evidence supporting regeneration after acquired tooth loss due to trauma or disease is still limited. The potential application of anti-USAG-1 therapy to acquired tooth loss, therefore, should be viewed as a translational hypothesis rather than an experimentally validated therapeutic outcome. Further studies in suitable models of acquired tooth loss are necessary to determine if this approach can be effective in inducing tooth regeneration in this context.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1.
authors: Wu Z, Ma Y, Li X, Yan Z, Huang Y, Wang K, Quan W, Mo L
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors.

title: A genetic engineering toolkit for the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii.
authors: Dong H, Xiao C, Zhang Y
abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii (S. boulardii) is the only yeast probiotic widely used in clinical practice and consumer products. It combines gastrointestinal robustness, intrinsic antibiotic tolerance and eukaryotic protein-processing capacity, making it an attractive chassis for engineered probiotics, in situ biomanufacturing and live biotherapeutic delivery. However, host-specific characterization of regulatory elements, candidate genomic integration sites, and multicopy integration strategies remains limited in the clinically used S. boulardii CNCM I-745 background. Here, using S. boulardii CNCM I-745 as the host, we developed and characterized a genetic engineering toolkit that integrates transcriptional control elements with genome-integration strategies. We first quantified the activities of 20 endogenous constitutive promoters, two inducible promoters and six terminators. We then established a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow and evaluated 10 chromosomal integration loci; six of which showed Editing efficiency above 80% while supporting comparable transgene expression without detectable growth penalties. Finally, we constructed an rDNA-repeat-based multicopy integration system that increased transgene expression by 9.8- to 22.6-fold relative to single-copy integration and revealed a significant positive but non-proportional association between estimated copy number and reporter output. Together, this toolkit provides S. boulardii with a set of tunable promoters and terminators, candidate chromosomal integration sites compatible with a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow. These resources expand the genetic accessibility of this probiotic yeast and provide a foundation for developing engineered S. boulardii strains with enhanced probiotic, therapeutic and biomanufacturing functions.

title: Unlocking genetic accessibility in Halomonas bluephagenesis: A high-efficiency transformation chassis enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing.
authors: Xu T, Guo F, Xiang H, Han J
abstract: Halomonas bluephagenesis has emerged as a promising chassis for industrial biotechnology distinguished by its halophilic robustness and capacity for open and continuous fermentation. However, its poor transformability has substantially limited rapid, iterative, and automatable strain engineering. Here, we develop a "restriction release" strategy that increases transformation efficiency from approximately 102 to 107 cfu/μg DNA, rivaling the efficiency of standard laboratory Escherichia coli. A spontaneous IS30 insertion disrupting the type II restriction endonuclease gene notI increased plasmid transformation efficiency by about 2000-fold. Targeted deletion of notI reproduced this phenotype, confirming its role as a major barrier. Further deletion of the DNA phosphorothioation restriction locus dptFGH yielded an additional 10 to 37-fold improvement, generating the highly transformable ΔEPSΔFlgΔNotIΔPTRes chassis. Notably, the enhanced chassis further facilitated two linear-DNA-based editing strategies: direct RecET-mediated pyrF deletion using a linear donor coupled with phenotypic selection, achieving a recombination efficiency of 16.7%, and CRISPR/Cas9-assisted ribDHBA promoter replacement via co-delivery of a gRNA plasmid and a linear donor, achieving an efficiency of 11.1%. Together, these results identify endogenous restriction systems as primary barriers to genetic manipulation in H. bluephagenesis. Stepwise restriction release markedly improves plasmid transformation and enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing, providing an improved genetic platform for the iterative engineering of this industrial halophile. More broadly, this study suggests a practical strategy for overcoming the genetic inaccessibility of other non-model microorganisms and accelerating iterative strain engineering.

title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Yu L, Li X, Huang L
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

title: SerpinE3 is a novel endogenous regulator of inflammation via TMPRSS11E inhibition.
authors: Zhang W, Chen Z, Han H, Bu Z, Liu L, Qiu H, Li S
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Although SerpinE3, an extracellular serine protease inhibitor, has been documented in several studies, its biological function remains largely undefined. In a screen for interactors of TMPRSS11E-a protease known to exacerbate inflammation and lung injury during infection-we identified a novel interaction with SerpinE3. Initially, we assessed the inhibitory effect of SerpinE3 on TMPRSS11E activity using synthetic fluorescent substrates PAR1 and PAR2 peptides. We further characterized SerpinE3 expression patterns in mouse cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) models of inflammation and in patients with pneumonia. Subsequently, the anti-inflammatory effects of SerpinE3 were investigated in both in vitro and in vivo inflammatory models. Finally, we examined the regulatory mechanisms governing SerpinE3 expression via promoter activity assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA). Our results demonstrate that SerpinE3 directly inhibits TMPRSS11E activity. SerpinE3 expression was significantly upregulated in alveolar and liver macrophages under inflammatory conditions. Administration of recombinant SerpinE3 protein markedly alleviated inflammation and acute lung injury in the mouse CLP model. Conversely, SerpinE3 knockout mice exhibited aggravated lung injury, a phenotype that was rescued by recombinant protein administration. Notably, aged SerpinE3 knockout mice displayed a spontaneous accumulation of inflammatory cells in the lungs. Mechanistically, we identified a functional NF-κB response element within the proximal promoter of SerpinE3. In conclusion, we identify SerpinE3 as an infection-inducible, macrophage-derived regulator that attenuates inflammatory lung injury, likely through the inhibition of TMPRSS11E. This study elucidates a critical anti-inflammatory role for SerpinE3 and paves the way for developing SerpinE3-based therapies for inflammatory acute lung injury.

Systems pharmacology reveals the molecular mechanisms of nerolidol against polycystic ovary syndrome through integrated transcriptomic, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Kumar GS, Soni A, Pattanayak N, Morie F, Baldaniya LH
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder marked by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation and oxidative stress, arising from dysregulation across several interconnected molecular pathways. Because its pathogenesis is multifactorial, therapies targeting diverse biological processes at once remain scarce. Nerolidol, a naturally occurring sesquiterpene alcohol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, has an action against PCOS whose molecular basis remains unresolved. Transcriptomic differences associated with PCOS were examined using the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE34526. Exploratory differential-expression screening identified nominally altered probes using an unadjusted P < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1; however, no individual probe remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR < 0.05. Functional enrichment analysis was subsequently used to investigate biological processes and pathways represented by these exploratory transcriptional signals. Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment were applied to pinpoint dysregulated biological processes and signalling pathways. Computational findings were tested in a letrozole-induced PCOS rat model treated with nerolidol, with efficacy judged from oestrous cyclicity, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormone profiles, oxidative stress biomarkers, inflammatory mediators and metabolic parameters. Transcriptomic analysis showed marked enrichment of processes related to kinase regulation, insulin secretion, intrinsic apoptotic signalling, receptor-mediated signalling and the DNA damage response, while KEGG analysis pointed to pathways governing endocrine regulation, cell signalling and metabolic homeostasis. In animal experiments, nerolidol restored oestrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, corrected endocrine disturbances, and reduced oxidative stress and PCOS-related pathology. These phenotypic effects were functionally concordant with several biological processes highlighted by the computational analyses. However, because the predicted signalling molecules and pathways were not directly measured in ovarian tissue following nerolidol treatment, the proposed molecular mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring targeted experimental validation.

Microfluidic integrated nucleic acid test (MINT) enabled by coupling FEN1-aided RPA with wax-purification and bead-carrier.
authors: Xu Z, Gao X, Huang J, Pang S, Wang S, Wang Y, Feng L, Ma Y
abstract: To guide timely antibiotic treatment, a tool for quick antimicrobial resistance gene detection is required. Here a Microfluidic Integrated Nucleic Acid Test platform (namely, MINT) was proposed for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. The platform integrates fast nucleic acid extraction based on hybrid wax-phase purification, and DNA amplification based on our newly developed FEN1-aided RPA (FARPA) into a microfluidic chip. The wax-phase stays solid at room temperature, while becomes liquid at >50 °C to allow the wash of inhibitors carried from extraction buffer, thus the chip keeps stable during storage and transportation. The movement of extracted DNA bound with magnetic beads were controlled by a magnet. The beaded DNA was quickly purified during the flow through the wax phase, and the amplification started once the beaded DNA reached to the well for FARPA. The signal from target-positive sample could be readily sensed by a conventional smartphone. The turnaround time is about 40 min from the sample to the result. The platform was validated by detecting the blaKPC-2 resistance gene of Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) from urine samples with the reliable detection concentration of 500 CFU/mL, achieving 100% agreement for the 29 clinical urine samples (19 positive, 10 negative) with conventional qPCR. It is easy to adapt the MINT to any other pathogen only by designing the corresponding primers and probes for FARPA. It is promising to apply MINT for bed-site antimicrobial resistance screening just after operation.

title: Oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum DNA among transgender women and travestis with high-titre syphilis in Brazil: findings from the MyTTrA study.
authors: Salle R, McCartney DJ, Grange PA, Mee P, Costa S, Magno L, Berçot B, de Sousa Mascena Veras MA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on transgender women and travestis (TGW) concerning oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum (TP) DNA are lacking. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of oral and anal TP DNA detection and the frequency of azithromycin resistance-associated mutations among TGW with high-titre syphilis in Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a nested cross-sectional study as part of the TransOdara study among TGW in five Brazilian cities. Participants with high-titre syphilis (reactive treponemal test and VDRL titre ≥1:8) and an analysable oral or anal specimen underwent quantitative PCR targeting the tpp47 and polA genes to detect TP DNA. TP DNA-positive specimens were further analysed using nested PCR and Sanger sequencing to identify mutations associated with azithromycin resistance. FINDINGS: Among the 249 participants with high-titre serological syphilis and analysable sample, TP DNA was detected in 25 (10.0%, 95% CI 6.6-14.5): 14 (5.6%) from the oral site only, 6 (2.4%) from the anal site only, and 5 (2.0%) from both sites. Participants in whom TP DNA was detected were younger and more frequently reported STI symptoms and anogenital ulcers during the preceding six months. The detection rate increased with VDRL titre (odds ratio 2.44, 95% CI 1.74-3.41 per doubling of titre for any oral or anal detection). Mutations associated with azithromycin resistance were observed in 76% (19/25, 95% CI 54.9-90.6) of participants in whom TP was detected. INTERPRETATION: TP DNA was detected in 10% of participants with high-titre serological syphilis. Detection increased with higher VDRL titres, supporting an association between higher non-treponemal titres and mucosal TP DNA detection. These findings support continued epidemiological and molecular surveillance of syphilis and of azithromycin resistance in transgender populations. They do not support site-specific PCR screening: syphilis diagnosis remains serological, and benzathine benzylpenicillin G remains the treatment of choice. FUNDING: French National Agency for Research on AIDS, Viral Hepatitis, and Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS/MIE).

title: From individual-based models to macroscopic dynamics of antimicrobial resistance.
authors: Menale M, Toscani G, Zanella M
abstract: We introduce and discuss a kinetic framework describing the time evolution of the statistical distributions of a population divided into the compartments of susceptible, infectious, recovered, and resistant in the presence of a microbial infection driven by susceptible-infectious interactions. Our main objective is to quantify the impact of excessive and inappropriate antimicrobial use, which accelerates the spread of resistance by enabling a fraction of infectious individuals to transition into the resistant compartment. The model consists of a system of Boltzmann-type equations capturing binary interactions between susceptible and infectious individuals, complemented by linear redistribution operators that represent recovery, the development of resistance, and reinfection processes. In the grazing-collision limit, we show that this Boltzmann system is well approximated by a system of coupled Fokker-Planck equations. This limiting description allows for a more tractable analysis of the dynamics, including the characterization of the long-time behavior of the population densities. Our analysis highlights how interaction terms drive the system toward a stable equilibrium and quantifies the effects of inappropriate antimicrobial use on the distribution of resistant individuals. Overall, the results offer a multi-scale perspective that bridges kinetic theory with classical epidemic modeling.

title: Integrated profiling of β-lactam susceptibility and spoilage-associated enzyme activities in psychrotrophic bacteria from the raw milk production chain.
authors: Hu X, Lei Y, Kong Z, Pang X, Shen J, Wang S
abstract: Psychrotrophic bacteria are important targets for microbiological control of cold-chain raw milk because of their ability to produce spoilage-associated enzymes and harbor antimicrobial resistance determinants. However, these two functional characteristics are often investigated separately, leaving their co-occurrence within the same isolate collection insufficiently characterized. To address this gap, 543 dominant culturable bacterial isolates were recovered from raw milk and dairy-farm-associated samples collected from six regions of China. Pseudomonas was the most prevalent genus, followed by Acinetobacter, Chryseobacterium, Serratia, and Psychrobacter. β-Lactam minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) distributions varied substantially among genera, with Chryseobacterium exhibiting the highest proportion of β-lactamase-associated phenotype-positive isolates. Among 226 raw-milk isolates screened using ceftazidime, all 44 isolates showing inhibitor-responsive or carbapenemase-associated phenotypes were subjected to whole-genome sequencing. Genome-wide resistance-gene screening identified annotated β-lactamase genes predominantly in Chryseobacterium and Acinetobacter. In contrast, the resistance-related annotations retained in phenotype-positive Pseudomonas isolates were mainly associated with efflux systems and adaptive response mechanisms. In the integrated analysis, a relative MIC-enzyme risk-prioritization score ranked Serratia (0.88), Chryseobacterium (0.71), and Pseudomonas (0.67) as the three highest-ranking genera. The β-lactam MIC score showed weak positive correlations with the protease-associated score (Spearman's ρ = 0.297, P < 0.001) and with the lipase-associated score (ρ = 0.194, P < 0.001). These findings indicate that genus abundance alone is insufficient to characterize the functional heterogeneity of psychrotrophic bacteria in raw milk. Integrating β-lactam MIC patterns with spoilage-enzyme activity provides complementary information for genus-level prioritization within this isolate collection.

Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Platinum-based Nanozyme screening coupled with ISAR-generated pyrophosphate for dual-mode detection of cardiovascular disease-associated miRNA-21.
authors: Chen M, Zhu J, Xu L, Liu W, Qi D
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Early assessment of cardiovascular disease (CVD)-associated molecular alterations may provide valuable information for disease monitoring and clinical evaluation. MicroRNA-21 (miRNA-21) is involved in multiple cardiovascular pathological processes and has been widely investigated as a CVD-associated circulating biomarker. Rationally modulating the activity of platinum-based nanozymes can expand sensing strategies and improve the performance of miRNA-21 detection. Herein, four platinum-based nanozymes are synthesized via a one-step reduction method and systematically evaluate their peroxidase (POD)-like catalytic activities. Among them, the NiPt nanozyme exhibits a favorable apparent peroxidase-like activity under an equal mass concentration, with the lowest Michaelis-Menten constant of 0.462 mM. Then, a colorimetric and fluorescent dual-mode biosensor is developed for the rapid and sensitive detection of miRNA-21 via NiPt nanozyme couple with the target-triggered invading stacking primer-based amplification reaction (ISAR). Sequence-specific hybridization between miRNA-21 and the designed hairpin DNA probe initiates ISAR and generates pyrophosphate (PPi), which suppresses the peroxidase-like activity of NiPt NPs and enables fast, instrument-free, and colorimetric qualitative detection of miRNA-21 at 5 × 10-11 M. Simultaneously, the Cy5 fluorescence signal exhibits sensitive quantitative detection of miRNA-21 with a limit of detection (LOD) of 2.27 × 10-13 M over a linear range of 10-12-10-9 M (R2 = 0.971). The biosensor demonstrated high selectivity toward miRNA-21 against representative interfering miRNA sequences and showed consistency with qRT-PCR in clinical serum samples from heart failure patients and healthy individuals. This dual-mode platform provides a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for miRNA-21 detection, demonstrating potential utility for CVD-associated biomarker analysis and further clinical investigation.

title: Long-term trajectories of invasive hemodynamic parameters and clinical outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation.
authors: Legtenberg S, Ter Maaten JM, Erasmus ME, Kuijpers M, Douglas YL, Droogh JM, de Felice E, van den Broek SAJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term hemodynamic changes after durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation are not well characterized. Characterizing these trajectories is clinically relevant, as persistent or evolving abnormalities in filling pressures and pulmonary circulation may identify patients at risk for adverse outcomes. METHOD: We conducted a retrospective single-center study including all patients who underwent durable LVAD implantation at the University Medical Center Groningen (2012 to 2025). We evaluated serial right heart catheterization (RHC) measurements to describe hemodynamic trajectories. Repeated measures, mixed-effect models were used to analyze hemodynamic trajectories up to 60 months of follow-up, including mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), right atrial pressure (RAP), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). Trajectories were compared according to survivor status, baseline LVAD strategy, development of late right ventricular failure (RVF), presence of aortic regurgitation (AR), and worsening renal function (WRF). RESULTS: Among 199 patients (176 HeartMate 3; 23 HeartMate II), mean PAP (-10.1 mmHg, 95% CI -13.1 to -7.1) and PCWP (-9.9 mmHg, 95% CI -12.5 to -7.2) decreased significantly within the first 6 months after LVAD implantation, while RAP (0.0 mmHg, 95% CI -0.8 to 0.8) remained unchanged. Cardiac index (+0.6 L/min/m², 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and cardiac output (+1.3 L/min, 95% CI 0.9-1.7) increased significantly over the same interval. Beyond 6 months, trajectories for most hemodynamic parameters remained generally stable. Non-survivors and patients developing late RVF showed consistently higher filling pressures with trajectories largely parallel to those of survivors or those without RVF. Hemodynamic trajectories did not differ by initial LVAD strategy. In contrast, clinically significant aortic regurgitation and WRF were associated with distinct hemodynamic trajectories. CONCLUSION: Hemodynamic parameters after durable LVAD implantation improved early and remained largely stable thereafter. Patients with adverse clinical outcomes showed persistently higher and/or altered hemodynamic profiles. These findings suggest that longitudinal hemodynamic assessment may enable early identification of patients at risk for adverse outcomes.

title: Disentangle to create: Architecture-level disentangled diffusion model for few-shot Chinese font generation.
authors: Li J, Yang S, Zhao J, Shen F
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Few-shot Chinese font generation aims to synthesize new characters in a target style using only a handful of reference images. Achieving accurate content rendering and faithful style transfer requires effective disentanglement between content and style. However, most existing approaches achieve only feature-level disentanglement and allow the generator to re-entangle these features, leading to content distortion and degraded style fidelity. To address this, we propose the Architecture-Level Disentangled Diffusion Model (ALD-Font) with an asymmetric design. The U-Net backbone takes SimSun-style glyphs as content templates, concatenated with noisy latents to construct a spatial canvas. Style features extracted from target-style images are injected as modulation signals to guide generation. Based on theoretical validation of disentanglement effectiveness, we adopt a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategy that updates only the style-related modules. This allows the model to better adapt to new styles while avoiding overfitting to the reference images' content under the few-shot setting. Additionally, we train a Background Noise Removal (BNR) module in the pixel space to remove background noise in complex stroke regions. We further introduce the Grey and OCR metrics to evaluate the content quality of generated characters. Experimental results show that ALD-Font achieves significantly higher style fidelity while maintaining comparable content accuracy to existing state-of-the-art methods. The implementation is available at https://github.com/JayLee1002/ALD-Font.

title: Transient gait instability during the initial phase of the 6-minute walk test in people with stroke: A nonlinear analysis using inertial measurement units.
authors: Inui Y, Takamura Y, Morioka S
abstract: BACKGROUND: In people with stroke (PwS), reduced gait speed and trunk acceleration changes in the latter half of the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) have been reported as fatigue-related, but temporal changes in motor control remain understudied. Clinicians often observe instability immediately after gait onset, yet quantitative evidence is scarce. This study used inertial measurement units (IMUs) and nonlinear analysis to examine fatigue-related changes and post-onset instability during the 6MWT in PwS. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 19 PwS and 19 age-matched controls completed the 6MWT wearing IMUs at the L5 vertebra and both ankles. Spatiotemporal parameters and stability indices (root mean square, harmonic ratio, sample entropy, short-term Lyapunov exponent [sLE]) were calculated. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) analyzed the 6-minute period both continuously and by comparing an initial phase (first 60 s) with the subsequent phase. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses were also performed. RESULTS: Continuous-time LMMs showed reduced cadence and increased double-support ratio in PwS. Among stability indices, only mediolateral sLE (sLE-ML) showed a significant group × phase interaction: increasing in the initial phase in PwS but not in controls. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses confirmed this finding was robust and specific to the 60-second cutoff. Initial-phase sLE-ML correlated negatively with Fugl-Meyer lower-extremity scores. CONCLUSIONS: PwS showed fatigue-related gait changes during the 6MWT, while mediolateral local dynamic stability transiently declined during the first 60 s before stabilizing. This instability was associated with motor paralysis, suggesting trunk IMU-based sLE-ML may reveal motor control deficits not captured by walking distance or speed.

From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
authors: Peng S, Liu Q, Duan C, Liu J, Wang R, Huang Y, Long A, Deng Q
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title: MHC class II deficiency in Algeria: Delineating the clinical, immunological, and genetic spectrum.
authors: Tahiat A, Cuollo L, Buta Panov S, Hakem S, Touri S, Saad-Djaballah A, Bendahmane C, Ketfi A
abstract: MHC class II deficiency is the most frequent combined immunodeficiency (CID) in the Maghreb, yet its phenotypic and molecular spectrum remains incompletely defined. Herein, we characterized 46 Algerian patients at the clinical, immunologic, and molecular levels. Disease onset was typically early, with a median age of 4.5 mo, while the clinical course was highly heterogeneous, ranging from severe, rapidly progressive disease to milder phenotypes with survival into adulthood. Recurrent infections were a universal feature, with protracted diarrhea (80.4%), recurrent pneumonia (71.7%), and oral candidiasis (54.3%) being the most common manifestations. CD4 lymphopenia occurred in 87% of patients, although lymphocyte profiles ranged from near-normal to SCID-like. Absent or nearly absent HLA-DR expression on both B cells and monocytes was observed in 44 patients, while two exhibited residual HLA-DR expression on B cells. Among 35 genetically characterized patients, 30 (85.7%) carried the recurrent RFXANK c.338-25_338del26 founder variant, while additional variants in RFXANK, RFXAP, and CIITA further broadened the molecular spectrum.

title: Population attributable mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada: a population-based ecological analysis.
authors: Fisman DN, Grima AA, Wilson NJ, Mann S, Tuite AR, Lee CE
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this. We estimated the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada, over 1993-2025, across the pandemic transition. METHODS: We analysed monthly all-cause mortality with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, influenza B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fitted for pre-pandemic (1993-2020) and combined pandemic (2020-2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions. Further analyses examined temporal stratification, exclusion of the early pandemic period, and models without Fourier adjustment. FINDINGS: Pre-pandemic, influenza A was associated with 1.8% (95% CI 1.4-2.3) of mortality; influenza B showed no association; RSV showed positive associations (1.9%, 1.3-2.4) only without seasonal adjustment. Amid elevated pandemic mortality (IRR 1.052, p < 0.0001), SARS-CoV-2 was associated with 6.48% (4.5-8.4) of deaths, 3-4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden. Attributable deaths (18,052) fell within 3% of 18,594 independently adjudicated Ontario COVID-19 deaths. Post-Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) SARS-CoV-2 mortality (9.8%, 1.1-17.7) did not differ from PHEIC estimates; post-PHEIC influenza did not differ from pre-pandemic baselines. INTERPRETATION: SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3-4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures, and continued to contribute beyond the formal emergency period, underscoring the importance of sustained respiratory virus prevention. FUNDING: Canadian Institutes of Health Research.
